question.problem:
If the function $f(x)=3{log}_{2}⁡(\frac{x-1}{3})-k?$ has an inverse function given by

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=3\cdot {2}^{(x+6)/3}+1,
$$

what is the value of $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y=3{log}_{2}⁡(\frac{x-1}{3})-k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x=3{log}_{2}⁡(\frac{y-1}{3})-k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3{log}_{2}⁡(\frac{y-1}{3})-k \\ 3{log}_{2}⁡(\frac{y-1}{3}) & =x+k \\ {log}_{2}⁡(\frac{y-1}{3}) & =\frac{x+k}{3} \\ {2}^{{log}_{2}⁡((y-1)/3)} & ={2}^{(x+k)/3} \\ \frac{y-1}{3} & ={2}^{(x+k)/3} \\ y-1 & =3\cdot {2}^{(x+k)/3} \\ y & =3\cdot {2}^{(x+k)/3}+1\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=3\cdot {2}^{(x+k)/3}+1.$ 

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=6.$
